challenges.name: dto-validation-quiz
challenges.title: Where does the check really happen?
challenges.description: Two requests to the CodeDev API after the team added DTOs and a global ValidationPipe: one rejected body, and one route parameter typed as a number. Decide whether each statement is True or False.

questions.explanation: True. Pipes run after guards and before the route handler. The ValidationPipe turns the body into an EnrollRequestDto, runs the class-validator decorators, and throws a BadRequestException with the list of messages when any check fails, so the handler - and the service it calls - never runs. The missing log line is the evidence. The message array and the 400 status are the ValidationPipe's default response; a common misconception is that the service produced this error and therefore still needs the same shape checks.

False. TypeScript types are erased when the code is compiled; at runtime every route parameter arrives as a string, and the log line says typeof id = string. Nest only converts it when you ask: ParseIntPipe on the parameter (@Param('id', ParseIntPipe)), or ValidationPipe({ transform: true }), which converts primitives based on the declared type. Without that, id === 42 is false and code such as id + 1 gives "421". The misconception is that a type annotation is a runtime check or conversion.

challenges.name: validate-enroll-request
challenges.title: Validate an enrollment request at the edge
challenges.description:
POST /v1/enrollments on CodeDev must reject bad input before EnrollmentService runs, and report every bad field at once so the form can highlight them all. Write validateEnrollRequest(body) in plain TypeScript - the same checks an EnrollRequestDto with class-validator decorators would make.

body is the parsed JSON body (any JSON value). Return { ok: true, value } when every field is valid, otherwise { ok: false, errors } where errors lists every invalid field once, in this order: courseId, email, plan, referralCode. Each error is { field, code }.

A field is missing when it is absent or null. code is "required" for a missing required field and "invalid" for a value that is present but has the wrong type or format.
- courseId (required): a string of 3 to 64 characters made of groups of lowercase letters a-z and digits joined by single hyphens, such as "sql-data-modeling" or "nodejs-101". No leading, trailing or double hyphens; not trimmed.
- email (required): a string. Trim surrounding whitespace first; then it must contain no whitespace, exactly one "@", at least one character before the "@", and after it a domain with at least one dot, where every part between dots is non-empty. The cleaned value is the trimmed email in lowercase.
- plan (required): exactly "free" or "premium" (case-sensitive).
- referralCode (optional): missing is fine and it is then left out of the value; otherwise a string of 6 to 12 characters, uppercase letters A-Z and digits only.

value has the keys courseId, email (cleaned), plan, and referralCode only when it was given. When the body is not a JSON object (an array, a number...), return { ok: false, errors: [{ field: "body", code: "invalid" }] }. The test runner prints the result as JSON.
hints: If you return as soon as you find the first bad field, how many round trips does a learner need to fix a form with three mistakes? And where does the order of the errors come from - the body, or the rules?

Check the fields one after another in the fixed order and push into one errors array. For each field ask two questions in this order: is it missing (undefined or null)? If not, is it the right type and format? A missing optional field is simply skipped. Build the cleaned value only when the array is empty.

The same pattern on a different form: a profile update with displayName (required, 2 to 40 characters, trimmed) and timezone (optional). For { "timezone": 7 } the result is [{ field: "displayName", code: "required" }, { field: "timezone", code: "invalid" }]: displayName comes first because the rules list it first, even though the body only contains timezone.

tests.name: A valid body with a referral code: the email is trimmed and lowercased
A missing email and an unknown plan give two errors in field order
Every field invalid: four errors in the fixed order, not the order of the body's keys
Without a referral code the value has exactly three keys
A null referral code counts as missing and is left out
A body that is a JSON array is rejected as a whole
Double hyphen in courseId, two @ in email, 13-character referral code are all invalid
null required fields are required; a blank email is present but invalid
